rubrics.text: More reverences to the earth are appointed for the Great Fast (Lent) than for the services at other seasons, and the penitential character of the Offices is augmented.
And if it be the Great Fast, we make three great reverences to the earth, reciting the prescribed Prayer of St. Ephraim the Syrian.
And if it be the Great Fast (Lent), we make three great reverences, reciting the prescribed Prayer of St. Ephraim the Syrian.
And if it be a Fast, we make three great reverences to the very earth and say the prescribed Prayer of St. Ephraim the Syrian.
Then twelve lesser reverences, saying at each: O God, cleanse thou me, a sinner. Then the whole Prayer is repeated; with one great reverence in conclusion.
On the Eve of Lazarus's Saturday the Great Fast proper (called "the Forty Days") comes to an end
